history.summary: Ardhnarishwar Temple in Mandi is an ASI-managed shrine to the composite Shiva-Parvati form, best known for its roofless (open-sky) mandapa. Sources genuinely diverge on three points: (1) the builder/age — aguidetohimachal cites 16th century under Raja Ajbar Sen or 17th century under Raja Sidh Sen (disputed), while lightuptemples claims 1000 years old (conflict, unsupported); (2) the missing roof has three rival explanations — deliberate theological symbolism (the masculine temple form left open to feminine sky), the legend that it is the unfinished 81st temple of the Pandavas' single-night building race, and the documented prosaic account that the maha-mandapa roof collapsed and preservation is poor; (3) a low-quality exam-prep source confuses it with the Bhootnath Temple and places others near Manali/Kangra, which should be disregarded. The stone composite image shows Shiva's right half (knotted hair, skull necklace, serpent, damru) and Parvati's left half (diadem, earring, nosering), with the bull and lion vehicles on an adjoining slab. The CSV spelling 'Ardhnareshwar' is corrected to the documented 'Ardhnarishwar'. Coordinates are POI-matched from map.geocode.

name: Ardhnarishwar Temple
town_description: Mandi is a historic town on the Beas River and the headquarters of Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. Known as 'Chhoti Kashi' (Varanasi of the Hills), it hosts some 81 old temples and is the venue of the famous Mandi Shivaratri Fair.

travel.railway: Joginder Nagar (narrow gauge) and Shimla (narrow gauge); broad-gauge connections at Chandigarh/Kalka
travel.road: In Mandi town, reachable by road from the main bazaar

visitor_information.opening_hours: Not verified in sources; temple accessible during daytime hours
